Incorporating SLOOS insights shifts the balance modestly more positive than the FSR-only take:

- Credit supply and demand: Banks eased standards across C&I and many CRE categories and reported stronger C&I demand from large, middle‑market, and small firms, with increased credit line inquiries. Easing was driven by improved economic outlook, competition, greater risk tolerance, and strong liquidity/capital. Banks also expected improvements in business and non-syndicated C&I lending, as well as CRE, construction, and land development loans.
- Household side: Banks reported weaker demand for residential real estate loans and expected deterioration in household credit (credit card, auto, and nonconforming jumbo), which, alongside rising rates, tempers the outlook for consumer-driven segments.
- Policy backdrop: The Fed’s hawkish pivot (imminent rate hikes, taper to end) still tightens the expected policy path, but SLOOS indicates bank intermediation remains supportive for business activity in the near term.

Net effect: Compared with the prior 0.05 score anchored by the FSR, SLOOS suggests stronger near-term support from bank credit to firms, partly offset by consumer headwinds and higher rates. Adjusting upward to mildly positive.
